prompt: A data set of $20$ test scores has a mean of $75$ and a median of $76$. One additional score of $12$ is added to the set. Which best describes the effect on the mean and the median?

choices.label: The mean decreases substantially; the median changes little
The median decreases substantially; the mean changes little

hint: Which measure uses every value, and which uses only position?

hints.text: Which measure uses every value, and which uses only position?
The mean sums all values, so an extreme value moves it. The median only shifts by one position.
The mean drops noticeably; the median barely moves.

learningObjective: Predict how an outlier affects the mean versus the median.
explanation: The mean is computed from the sum, so adding a value far below the others pulls it down: the new mean is $\dfrac{20(75) + 12}{21} = \dfrac{1512}{21} = 72$.
The median depends only on which value sits in the middle. Adding one low score shifts the middle position by half a slot, so the median moves at most a little.
This is what "the median is resistant to outliers" means.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why the median resists
steps: To move the median substantially, you would have to add many low values, not one.
The median does not care *how* low the new value is — only that it is below the middle.
Replacing that $12$ with a $0$ would change the mean again but leave the median exactly where it is.
